prompts.oscar:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: 12-frame transparent sprite sheet for a single non-looping fighting-game entrance.
Reference image: the supplied existing game atlas of Óscar D'León is the identity and costume lock. Preserve exactly his recognizable bald head, thick dark moustache, cheerful strong face, dark skin tone, black open satin overshirt, black tiger-print T-shirt, gold necklace, sparkly black trousers and black loafers. Match the detailed hand-painted retro fighting-game illustration style of this atlas.
Primary request: create ONE chronological action: he opens BOTH arms warmly and performs ONE complete 360-degree salsa dance turn on his feet, then settles in guard facing his opponent. This is not a repeating dance.
Layout: exactly TWELVE isolated full-body poses on genuine transparent alpha, FOUR equal columns by THREE equal rows, chronological left-to-right top-to-bottom. Prefer 2048x1536 or larger. All cells equal, safe transparent gaps, one consistent body scale, same planted-foot baseline, full fingers/arms/head/shoes visible; limbs never enter another cell. No background, floor, shadows, captions, numerals, effects, musical notes or grid lines. Hands are empty.
Frames: 0=initial three-quarter stance facing screen RIGHT, hands up gently exactly like reference guard; 1=both palms lower and start opening; 2=both arms extended wide in welcome, knees softly bent, smiling; 3=arms remain open, dance pivot begins toward camera, torso nearly front-facing; 4=quarter-turn, strict side profile facing LEFT; 5=three-quarter BACK view, same outfit, arms remain spread; 6=full BACK view half-turn (show back of bald head and plain back of black overshirt, no face on back); 7=other three-quarter BACK view; 8=side profile facing RIGHT; 9=three-quarter front view, coming back around; 10=completed full revolution, original three-quarter facing RIGHT with arms still open and happy face; 11=arms lower into original RIGHT-facing guard.
The rotation must be real anatomically correct views including back and both profiles, not rotated flat cutouts or mirrored copies. Only this same man, no other characters. Keep expression and proportions consistent.
prompts.dudamel:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: 12-frame transparent sprite sheet for a single non-looping fighting-game entrance.
Reference image: the supplied Gustavo Dudamel game atlas locks the identity, style and costume. Preserve his recognizable young face, broad friendly smile, thick curly dark hair, dark navy orchestral tailcoat and waistcoat, white shirt, dark tie, matching trousers, black shoes. He holds one thin STRAIGHT conducting baton in his RIGHT hand. Match the existing detailed hand-painted retro fighting-game art.
Primary request: ONE continuous conductor's invitation: slowly open both arms broadly to gather the orchestra, lift the baton once, conduct ONE decisive sweeping downbeat, then return to a calm opponent-facing ready stance. No repeating conducting beat.
Layout: exactly TWELVE isolated full-body poses on genuine transparent alpha, FOUR equal columns by THREE equal rows, chronological left-to-right top-to-bottom. Prefer 2048x1536 or larger. All cells equal, safe transparent gaps, consistent body height, same grounded foot baseline, full fingers/arms/baton/head/shoes visible. No background, orchestra, scenery, shadows, labels, numbers, musical notes, graphics, grid lines. Keep the original THREE-QUARTER facing screen RIGHT in all poses.
Frames: 0=original friendly ready stance like reference pose0, baton held in front; 1=elbows begin opening; 2=both arms half-open to either side; 3=both arms OPEN broadly at shoulder level, baton extended in right hand, left palm invites musicians; 4=arms still open as right hand begins rising, left palm gathers inward slightly; 5=right elbow and baton rising toward a high upbeat, left hand lifted openly; 6=single peak with right baton arm high, gaze alert and left hand poised; 7=decisive downbeat starting, right arm sweeps down and forward; 8=right baton low after sweeping down, slight forward torso emphasis, left hand brings orchestra in; 9=motion decelerates and arms relax; 10=hands gather calmly in front; 11=exact original three-quarter RIGHT-facing ready stance.
No punch/kick/jumping. One opening and one downbeat only; no alternate repeated high-low gestures. Baton stays straight and attached to his hand throughout. Preserve face/costume and stable camera/scale across frames.
